- Declared three stopping rules upfront (best_so_far_above 1.2 → stop, failures_at_least 3 → stop, last_gain_at_most 0.02 → restart), and a placeholder prior on feature 0 (no principled non-data basis existed, so it was meant to be overridden empirically).

- Iteratively extended and restarted across five independent anchors (features 32, 33, 18, 16, 19). Each time, feature 35 (short) emerged as the strongest complementary feature, but adding a third feature never improved on the best 2-feature combination.
- The best candidate found was **[33+, 35−]** with Sharpe 0.491 (all-years-equal) / 0.554 (recent-years-weighted) — consistently reproduced as the ceiling across multiple restarts, giving good confidence this is a robust local optimum rather than a lucky single draw.
- After repeated restarts failed to beat this candidate, I changed the trigger to stop on the first failure post-restart, judging further search unlikely to yield meaningful improvement and more likely to risk overfitting.

- Expected in-sample optimism/decay even from a modest, non-exhaustive search
- A simple, low-complexity rule (2 features, equal weight) that is less prone to overfitting than a highly tuned multi-feature combination
- Still expected to beat the baseline model's in-sample Sharpe (0.183/0.246) based on the consistency of the signal across independent anchors
